products.summary: A compressor air conditioner light enough to carry to a tent. The 22 lb unit and the 14 lb, 1,022 Wh battery are separate pieces, 36 lb in all. It gives 5,280 BTU of cooling and also heats.
products.fit: Tent campers who walk their gear from the car to the site, and owners of small vans or truck cabs who want to set it up without drilling.
caveats: One battery lasts about 5 to 7 hours in Sleep mode and 2 to 3 hours in Rocket mode, so a full hot night needs two batteries.
The AC runs on 48 V. A car's 12 V socket can recharge the battery but cannot run the AC.
The battery uses lithium-ion 21700 cells, not LFP.
There is no app. You control it with the buttons and the remote.
Less cooling than the EcoFlow Wave 3 (5,280 vs 6,100 BTU).

notes: Query choice: 'battery powered air conditioner for tent'. The pages ranking for it are mostly affiliate roundups (pickhvac, theatlasheart, fixr, nerdtechy, pwice) that mix real compressor units with misting fans, so the results are thin. Pain points, counted across the reviews and roundups read (GPX Adventures, PickHVAC, Digital Reviews Network, aboutdarwin, 4wdtalk, Trail and Kale/T3 snippets): one-battery runtime 5; bulk/weight 6 (Wave 3: 4wdtalk, aboutdarwin, T3 snippet 'roughly 55 lbs with battery'; Mark 3 trunk space: GPX, PickHVAC, DRN); price 4; noise for light sleepers 3; hose/duct setup 3; no app on Mark 3 2; evaporative 'battery AC' confusion 2. Segments and winners: (1) carry-in tent campers: Zero Breeze Mark 3 + 1 battery, 36 lb in two pieces vs about 55 lb for the Wave 3 + battery; (2) car-side campers who want maximum cooling: EcoFlow Wave 3 + add-on battery (6,100 vs 5,280 BTU, LFP, app). EcoFlow is not an approved program, so it gets a plain maker link and no {buy:} token; (3) all night without recharging: Mark 3 + 2 batteries. Mark 3 Basic is listed for owners of Mark 3 batteries. Verified 2026-11-10 with storecheck search on zerobreeze.com: Mark 3 + 1 battery $1,779 (compare-at $2,399), + 2 batteries $2,349 ($3,399), Basic AC only $1,219 ($1,399), Mark 3 battery $839, Mark 3 Care+ $129, all available. Also from store text: 5,280/5,800 BTU, 61-88 °F, 100-150 sq ft, 150 W min / 500 W cooling input, 48 V (38-58.5 V), 'just under 22 lb'; battery 1,022 Wh 21700 Li-ion, 14 lb, 12-60 V in, 0-80% about 2 h, chain up to 5, 12 V Anderson 120 W / USB-C 100 W / USB-A 18 W; the 12 V car cable only charges the battery and cannot run the AC; accessories excluded from the 30-day return policy. EcoFlow store search on 2026-11-10: Wave 3 add-on battery $649, 1,024 Wh LFP, 4,000 cycles. Could not verify, because zerobreeze.com pages, us.ecoflow.com product pages, storecheck product and WebFetch all returned HTTP 429 all session: (a) storecheck product variants for the Mark 3 listings; (b) Mark 3 warranty term (reviewers say 1 year; left off the page); (c) Mark 3 return eligibility (a search excerpt of zerobreeze.com/pages/return-policy says the 30-day money-back guarantee covers only the Mark 2, Mark 2 battery and ElecHive, so the Mark 3 may not be returnable; the page tells buyers to confirm); (d) what comes in the Mark 3 Basic box (PickHVAC says an AC adapter is included; not on the page); (e) the 46 dB noise rating (cited by reviewers, attributed to them on the page); (f) Mark 3 runtime by mode (5-7 h Sleep, 2-3 h Rocket) comes from the maker FAQ as quoted by GPX Adventures and PickHVAC, not read directly; (g) EcoFlow Wave 3 unit price, stock and weight. The unit did not appear in EcoFlow US store search today, so it may be sold out or hidden. The 33.7 lb unit / 21.4 lb battery weights and the 'up to 8 h' runtime come from retailer listings and reviews, not EcoFlow's page. The Wave 3 row carries no price; (h) US shipping restrictions (aboutdarwin says Zero Breeze can't ship to all locations; an older promo excerpt says contiguous US only). Brand-site codes: could not read the zerobreeze.com home page or banners (429 / truncated), so only the two Awin codes are listed. Rivals not tabled: CyberTake S2 Pro (5,100 BTU, no battery, needs a power station; maker US page not found) and Zero Breeze Mark 2 (the AC unit no longer appears in store search, only its battery and accessories). No Amazon records, per the temporary rule.
